axis_note: Assigned axis is bio per S0-DESIGN §3.1 (listed as a 공통조상 under '생물'). The object of study is a spiking neural network simulation, not an animal, so the paper is a COMPUTATIONAL model of a biological hypothesis, not an in-vivo measurement. Its biological warrant is entirely by citation to the sleep-consolidation literature [L627-635, L671-682], not by new biological data. Mechanically the paper is a Θ-path paper -- the deployed weight matrix is what changes -- but its role in the monograph is the biological grounding of the whole line (Part I module T6), and the strongest single existence proof in the corpus that an offline phase does something a wake phase cannot: it produces a two-task weight state that no amount of additional single-task wake training produces.

problem_stated.statement: Artificial neural networks trained sequentially on tasks overwrite the synaptic weights learned during the previous task, leaving the network incapable of performing the earlier task -- catastrophic forgetting [L54-57, L100-102]. The historical fix, interleaved training, works but 'imposes the stringent constraint that the original training data be perpetually stored for later use and combined with new data to retrain the network' [L109-111]. Hence the paper's operative problem, stated in one sentence: 'Thus, the challenge is to understand how the biological brain enables memory reactivation during sleep without access to past training data.' [L111-113]
problem_stated.operational_question: 'Can we implement a sleep like phase to our model to protect an old task and still accomplish new task learning without explicit re-training of the old task?' [L290-292]
problem_stated.hypothesis_tested: That a spiking network's local learning rules plus spike-based communication 'allow previously learned memory traces to reactivate spontaneously and modify synaptic weights without interference during off-line processing--sleep' [L114-117].
problem_stated.claimed_answer: Yes, and the geometric characterisation is the paper's actual contribution: sleep 'mitigated catastrophic forgetting by constraining the network synaptic weight state to the previously learned manifold, while allowing the weight configuration to converge towards the intersection of the manifolds representing old and new tasks' [Abstract L60-62].
problem_stated.source: Abstract L54-63; Introduction L97-140; Results L272-311

Therefore every potentiation is paid for by depression elsewhere in the same column: the update is a projected, zero-sum update, not free growth. The paper's own explanation of why sleep beats freezing rests on this -- 'the sleep phase results in a large cluster of weights being renormalized around an intermediate value of synaptic strength in the network' [L511-512]. core_mechanism.reduction_to_frame: Frame (U-Θ) reads Θ_{k+1} = Θ_k - η_Θ ∇_Θ L(R_k; Θ_k) with R_k = gen(H_k; B_s). This paper instantiates it as follows. (a) Θ = the 6272 excitatory hidden-to-output synapses (plus the derived inhibitory block and the frozen input-to-hidden block). (b) There is no L and no ∇: the descent direction is replaced by the local three-factor product of (T04-2), followed by the projection Π of (T04-6) onto the constant-column-sum set. (c) η_Θ has no separate existence -- the step size is folded into r, into K = ±0.04, and into Δ_tar. (d) R_k is not a dataset. It is the stream of spontaneous spike sequences that the network emits when layer H is driven by Poisson noise and layer O is left free to respond through Θ^{H→O}_k. Therefore gen(H_k; B_s) is literally 'run the network forward on noise for B_s movement cycles', and H_k -- the accumulated experience -- is stored NOWHERE except inside Θ_k itself. That is the claim the whole paper exists to demonstrate: 'Sleep makes this possible by replaying old memory traces without the explicit usage of the old task data.' [L94-95, restated L727]. (e) One extra scalar per hidden neuron does cross the wake→sleep boundary: the target Poisson rate \bar f_i, measured from wake firing statistics [L982-985]. The Uniform-Noise Sleep control collapses these 784 scalars to a single population mean and the result survives [S4E/F, L355-362, L1145-1150], so the irreducible carried state is 1 scalar.
core_mechanism.why_offline_is_necessary: The paper's mechanistic account, in its own words: 'Each episode of new Task 2 training improves Task 2 performance but damages synaptic connectivity responsible for old Task 1. If continuous Task 2 training is long enough, the damage to Task 1 becomes irreversible. Having a sleep phase after a short period of Task 2 training enables spontaneous forward replay between hidden and output layers (H->O) that preferentially benefits the strongest synapses. Thus, if Task 1 synapses are still strong enough to maintain replay, they are replayed and weights are increased.' [L307-311]. The offline phase is necessary because the replay it enables is IMPOSSIBLE during wake: during wake the input layer imposes the current task's statistics on layer H, so the H→O correlations that form are the new task's. Only when the sensory drive is removed and replaced by unstructured noise does the H→O weight matrix get to select which correlations appear -- i.e. the strongest surviving synapses win. That selection is a property of the weight matrix alone, which is exactly why no wake-time procedure reproduces it.

outer_vs_inner.readers_first_answer: NOTHING in this paper is learned by an outer loop, and there is no gradient descent anywhere. There is no differentiable loss, no backward pass, no optimizer, no meta-learning. Every object that moves does so by a local, online rule evaluated during either a wake movement cycle or a sleep movement cycle. The only things chosen by a human are hyperparameters. A reader coming from the rest of the corpus should hold this contrast fixed: in every other Θ-path paper the sleep round runs an optimizer over a constructed dataset; here the sleep round runs the network's own dynamics and lets a Hebbian rule plus a normalisation constraint do the work.

update_layer.instantiates: (U-Θ) ONLY -- twice per interleaved period, on the same parameter block, in alternation.
not_instantiated: (U-W): there is no fast-weight state. Nothing is carried between movement cycles except the weights themselves and the homeostatic scalars. W = ∅ throughout.

(U-E): there is no external store. The paper's entire point is to eliminate the stored-data buffer that interleaved training requires [L108-113, L673-677]. E = ∅ by construction, and the paper argues that E should be ∅.
update_layer.order_within_one_interleaved_period: The protocol is strictly alternating with a 1:1 duty cycle. One period k = [100 movement cycles of new-task wake training under (T04-2) with the environment present and r ∈ {1, -0.001, -0.0001}] followed by [100 movement cycles of sleep under (T04-4) with the environment empty, the input layer silent, layer H noise-driven, and r ≡ 0.5]. Both halves write the SAME Θ^{H→O}. The paper calls the composite protocol Interleaved_{S,T2} (sleep alternated with Task 2 training) or Interleaved_{S,T1} (sleep alternated with Task 1 training). [Results L300-306; Methods: Simulated sleep L985-986]
difference_from_canonical: The descent direction is not a gradient. ∇_Θ L is replaced by a local eligibility-trace-gated Hebbian product (T04-2). There is no loss function anywhere in the paper.

The update is PROJECTED after every event onto the set {Σ_i Θ_ij = Θ^0_{·j}} by heterosynaptic normalisation (T04-6). Canonical (U-Θ) has no such constraint. This projection is what makes the sleep round zero-sum and is, on the paper's own account, why sleep outperforms synapse freezing [L509-517].

R_k is generated by running the network itself on noise rather than by sampling, distilling or synthesising a dataset. gen(·; B_s) here = 'simulate B_s movement cycles of noise-driven spontaneous activity'. H_k has no storage location outside Θ_k -- there is no replay buffer, no generative model, no summary, no text.

The wake phase is ALSO (U-Θ). This is the structural fact that separates this paper from every deployment-oriented paper in the corpus: there is no frozen serving artefact. In LLM terms, wake-time inference here would be continuously fine-tuning the served weights.

η_Θ has no independent existence; there is no learning-rate schedule and no decay. The paper explicitly contrasts this with classical interleaved training, which 'can be ameliorated with a learning rate decay schedule' [L658-659].
update_layer.path_assignment_for_the_monograph: Θ-path by mechanism, bio by role. When the monograph writes the three-path table, this paper belongs in the Θ column -- the deployed weights change and nothing else exists -- but it must be introduced as a common ancestor, before the paths separate, alongside CLS and Deep Generative Replay.

cost_table.preamble: This is a 2022 computational-neuroscience paper. It reports NO computational cost of any kind: no FLOPs, no wall-clock, no CPU/GPU hours, no memory footprint, no energy. Three of the four cost cells are therefore 'absent'. That absence is itself the finding the monograph should report: the biological grounding of the sleep-time-compute line comes with zero cost accounting, so nothing in the amortization argument of frame Eq. (A) can be sourced to this paper.

B_s.value: PARTIAL -- stated only as simulated duration, never as compute.
B_s.detail: One sleep interval lasts 100 movement cycles, exactly equal to the new-task training interval that precedes it: 'alternating periods of training on Task 2 (new task) lasting 100 movement cycles and periods of "sleep" of the same duration' [L301-303], restated in Methods as 'alternating intervals of this sleep phase and training on Task 1, with each interval lasting 100 movement cycles (although no movement occurred)' [L985-986]. So the sleep:wake duty ratio is exactly 1:1 in simulated time. One movement cycle = one 'epoch' = 600 simulation timesteps [L769] at 0.5 ms per timestep [L807], i.e. ~300 ms of simulated time [L769]. ARITHMETIC ON STATED NUMBERS (not an estimate): one sleep interval = 100 x 600 = 60,000 neuron-update timesteps = ~30 s of simulated time. ABSENT: FLOPs, wall-clock, CPU-hours, energy, and -- importantly -- the NUMBER of interleaved periods run. The total duration of an Interleaved phase is never stated numerically in the text; the only time-axis number given is the annotation that Interleaved_{S,T1} begins at 240,000 aeons in the Fig 6A protocol [L453], with 1 aeon = 100 movement cycles [L199, L782-783] and 'Each simulation consisted of millions of these movement cycles / epochs' [L781].
B_s.source: Results L300-306; Methods: Policy L769, L776-783; Methods: Neuron models L807; Methods: Simulated sleep L985-986; Fig 6A L453
B_s.single_point_warning: B_s is a SINGLE POINT. There is no sweep over sleep duration, over the sleep:wake ratio, or over the number of interleavings. The paper reasons qualitatively about the regime boundary -- 'a single long episode of new task learning would push the network far away from the old task manifold making it impossible to recover by subsequent sleep' [L651-653] -- but never measures where that boundary is.

L_w.detail: No latency, throughput, time-to-first-anything or per-decision cost is reported anywhere in the paper. [INFERENCE, clearly marked] Structurally the wake path is unchanged by the existence of a sleep phase: a decision is one movement cycle of 600 timesteps through the fixed three-layer feedforward architecture [Methods: Policy L769-789], and sleep changes only the VALUES in Θ^{H→O}, never the architecture, the layer sizes or the per-decision work. So the sleep-time compute of this paper contributes exactly zero to wake-time latency -- but the paper never says this and never measures it.
L_w.source: absence throughout; structural basis Methods: Policy L768-796 and Methods: Simulated sleep L965-986

C_cap.value: absent in bytes -- no dtype, no byte count, no memory footprint is stated anywhere in the paper.
C_cap.detail: What the paper DOES state, in counts: 842 spiking map-based neurons in total [L743], arranged as a 7x7 input layer I (49 neurons, of which 48 receive a unique location input [L771]), a 28x28 hidden layer H (784 neurons), and a 3x3 output layer O with a nonfunctional centre neuron, i.e. 8 functional outputs [L744-746]. Each H neuron receives excitatory synapses from 9 randomly selected I neurons [L751] -- 784 x 9 = 7056 I→H synapses (arithmetic on stated numbers). Each H neuron connects to every O neuron with one excitatory and one inhibitory synapse [L753-755]. The excitatory H→O block is stated explicitly twice as 6272 dimensions [SVM training L995; distance function L1035]. The inhibitory block is the same size but carries zero degrees of freedom, being recomputed as the negative mean of each source neuron's excitatory outgoing weights [L956-963]. Auxiliary state: 8 homeostatic set-point scalars [L938-945], 784 fixed outgoing-sum targets [L928-930], and 784 measured target firing rates for the sleep drive [L982-985] -- the last collapsing to 1 scalar in the Uniform-Noise Sleep control [S4E/F L1145-1150].
C_cap.the_capacity_claim_that_matters: ZERO bytes of past-task data are retained. This is the paper's headline capacity result and it is stated three times: 'without the need to store and train on previous task data or environments' [L611]; 'the data intensive process of storing old data and using them for retraining can be avoided in SNN by implementing periods of noise-induced spontaneous reactivation during new task training' [L674-677]; 'Sleep makes this possible by replaying old memory traces without explicit usage of the old training data.' [L727]. The state that crosses the wake→sleep boundary is 784 scalars, reducible to 1.

rho.value: PARTIAL -- endpoint accuracies for ONE interfering task, never a per-round decay rate, and never more than two tasks.
rho.detail: Chance performance is 0.5 [L167]. Baseline after Task 1 training alone: Task 1 = 0.70 ± 0.02, Task 2 = 0.53 ± 0.02 [L228-229]. Under sequential T1→T2 the old task decays to chance: Task 1 = 0.52 ± 0.02 [L275]. Under Interleaved_{S,T2} the old task does not decay at all: Task 1 = 0.70 ± 0.03 [L304-305]. So over one interfering task, ρ(sequential) = 0.70 → 0.52, i.e. the entire 0.20-wide band between chance and trained performance is lost; ρ(sleep-interleaved) = 0.70 → 0.70, i.e. zero measured loss. A multi-round ρ -- the quantity the monograph actually needs, degradation per repeated sleep round over many tasks -- is ABSENT: the paper never runs a third task and never runs a second Interleaved phase.
rho.source: L167, L228-229, L275-276, L304-305; the two-task ceiling is stated at L164-165 and holds throughout

amortization_A.detail: Frame Eq. (A), C_avg = C_wake + C_sleep/N_q, requires N_q, the number of queries sharing one context. This paper has no query stream, no notion of a context, and no user. The agent emits one decision per movement cycle forever. The nearest quantity is the 1:1 sleep:wake duty ratio, which in Eq. (A) terms would say C_sleep = C_wake per period, but there is no N_q to divide by. The monograph must state that the biological ancestor of the line supplies NO amortization evidence.
amortization_A.source: structural; duty ratio from L301-303 and L985-986

experiments.trial_protocol: 'All reported results are based on at least 10 trials with different random network initialization.' [L168-169]. All reported numbers are mean ± standard deviation across those trials. NO statistical test, no p-value, and no confidence interval appears anywhere in the paper, although the word 'significantly' is used at least three times [L418, L444, L506].
experiments.task_definition: Two complementary complex foraging tasks in a 50x50 grid with 10% particle density [L731, L739]. Particles are two pixels long in one of four orientations: vertical, horizontal, positive diagonal, negative diagonal [L731-732]. Task 1: horizontal rewarded, negative diagonal punished. Task 2: vertical rewarded, positive diagonal punished [L225-226, L231-232, L932-935]. During training and testing only the two task-relevant orientations are present [L226-227, L734-735]. The performance metric is 'pattern discriminability (ratio of rewarded vs punished particles consumed)', with chance = 0.5 [L166-167]. The agent sees a 7x7 egocentric visual field and can move to any of eight adjacent squares [L739-740].

runs.setup: unsupervised period (all four orientations at equal density) → Task 1 reinforcement training. I→H frozen during RL.
runs.claim: 'The naive agent moved randomly through the environment (Fig 1D, left), but after task training, moved to seek out horizontal patterns and largely avoid negative diagonal ones' [L229-231]

runs.id: E2 -- Task 2 is learnable (the complementary task)
runs.section: Results L231-237, Fig 1C/1E; the number itself is quoted at L276 and L305
runs.numbers: Task 2 = 0.69 ± 0.03 [L276, restated L305]. The paper also writes 'single Task 1 (0.70 ± 002)' at L305 -- the standard deviation is misprinted in the source; the correct value from L228 is 0.70 ± 0.02.
runs.claim: 'These results demonstrate that the network is capable of learning and performing either one of the two complementary complex foraging tasks.' [L232-233]

runs.id: E3 -- CATASTROPHIC FORGETTING: sequential T1 → T2
runs.setup: Task 1 training, then Task 2 training with no interleaving and no sleep
runs.numbers: Task 1 = 0.52 ± 0.02 ('down to no better than chance'); Task 2 = 0.69 ± 0.03 [L275-276]
runs.claim: 'sequential training on a complementary task caused the network to undergo catastrophic forgetting of the task trained earlier, remembering only the most recent task' [L276-278]
runs.note: This is the negative control the whole paper is measured against.

runs.id: E4 -- BASELINE: classical interleaved training Interleaved_{T1,T2} (requires stored old-task data)
runs.setup: after Task 1 training, alternate short presentations of Task 1 and Task 2 every 100 movement cycles
runs.claim: 'interleaved training allowed the network to learn new Task 2 without forgetting previously learned Task 1. However ... it imposes the stringent constraint that all the original training data (in our case explicit access to the Task 1 environment) be stored' [L282-286]
runs.note: THIS IS THE STRONG BASELINE. It is data-hungry but it works, and its numbers are close to the sleep numbers.

runs.id: E5 -- HEADLINE RESULT: Interleaved_{S,T2} (sleep alternated with new-task training, NO old-task data)
runs.setup: Task 1 training, then alternating 100-movement-cycle periods of Task 2 training and 100-movement-cycle periods of sleep. 'Importantly, no training on Task 1 was performed at any time during InterleavedS,T2.' [L303-304]
runs.claim: 'comparable to single Task 1 (0.70 ± 002) or Task 2 (0.69 ± 0.03) performances (Fig 1B and 1C) and exceeding those achieved through InterleavedT1,T2 training (Fig 3C and 3D)' [L305-306]
runs.note: The 'exceeding' claim rests on 0.70 vs 0.68 on Task 1 and 0.68 vs 0.65 on Task 2, against standard deviations of 0.03-0.05, with no significance test reported. See unfavorable_facts.

runs.id: E6 -- CONTROL: does the sleep noise itself teach the task? Naive network + Interleaved_{S,T1} using Task 2 firing-rate statistics
runs.setup: A completely naive network is given Interleaved_{S,T1}, but the hidden-layer target firing rates used to shape the sleep noise were taken from a DIFFERENT experiment's post-Task-2 statistics -- deliberately leaking Task 2 information into the noise.
runs.claim: 'the network learns Task 1 but Task 2 performance remained at baseline' [L351-352]. Sleep noise carrying Task 2 rate statistics does not teach Task 2.
runs.note: Note that Task 1 reaches only 0.60 ± 0.03 here, below the 0.70 of E1 -- the paper does not comment on this shortfall.

runs.id: E7 -- CONTROL: Interleaved_{S,T1} applied after Task 1 training
runs.numbers: after Task 1 training: Task 1 = 0.70 ± 0.02, Task 2 = 0.53 ± 0.02. After Interleaved_{S,T1}: Task 1 = 0.71 ± 0.02, Task 2 = 0.51 ± 0.02 [L1141-1143]
runs.claim: 'it maintained performance on Task 1 but again without any performance gain for Task 2' [L353-354]
runs.note: The cleanest statement in the paper of what sleep does NOT do: it does not create knowledge that was never trained.

runs.id: E8 -- CONTROL: Uniform-Noise Sleep (US) -- one population-mean rate for all hidden neurons
runs.setup: Same as E5 but 'we used the same input firing rate for all hidden layer neurons determined by the mean firing of the entire hidden layer population as opposed to the private spiking history of individual H neurons' [L357-359]
runs.numbers: after Task 1 training: Task 1 = 0.70 ± 0.02, Task 2 = 0.53 ± 0.02. After the uniform-noise interleaved phase: Task 1 = 0.67 ± 0.05, Task 2 = 0.69 ± 0.03 [L1148-1150]
runs.claim: 'these results suggest that the properties of the input that drives firing during sleep are not essential to enable replay, any similar to awake random activity in layers H and O is sufficient to prevent forgetting' [L360-362]
runs.note: This is the control that reduces the wake→sleep carried state from 784 scalars to 1. It is the most important control in the paper for the monograph's capacity argument. Naming discrepancy: the Results text calls it Interleaved_{US,T1} [L359] while the S4 caption calls it Interleaved_{US,T2} [L1146]; the numbers show Task 2 was the trained task, so the Results label appears to be a typo.

runs.id: E9 -- BASELINE: freeze the top-x% of Task-1-relevant synapses instead of sleeping
runs.setup: Task 1 training, then Task 2 training with the strongest x% of post-Task-1 synapses held frozen. In all three cases the post-Task-1 baseline was Task 1 = 0.70 ± 0.02, Task 2 = 0.53 ± 0.02 [L1184].
runs.claim: 'in all cases, some degree of retroactive or prospective interference was observed highlighting the fact that the sleep-like phase performs a significantly more sophisticated modification to the weight matrix than simply freezing (or amplifying) task relevant synapses.' [L509-511]. The paper explicitly links freezing to Elastic Weight Consolidation: 'freezing a fraction of synaptic weights that are most relevant to old tasks (however, implemented in more complex form) is one of the approaches in machine learning to avoid catastrophic forgetting--Elastic Weight Consolidation [7].' [L517-547]
runs.note: This is the paper's cleanest quantitative win: freezing traces out a strict trade-off curve (1% → new task only; 10% → old task only; 5% → 0.65/0.61) whereas sleep reaches 0.70/0.68, dominating every freezing point on both axes simultaneously. EWC itself is NOT run -- only this hand-rolled freezing proxy.

runs.setup: progressively remove hidden-layer neurons at random during the testing period, starting from 784 and decreasing to 0 [L1108-1109]
runs.numbers: Main text: performance stays steady 'until around 70% of the hidden layer was pruned' [L240-241]. S2 caption: 'The testing performance remains high until ~25% of neurons are left, after which it starts to drop.' [L1109-1110]
runs.claim: 'Such high resiliency suggests the network utilizes a highly distributed coding strategy to develop its policy.' [L241-242]
runs.note: The two statements correspond to 70% removed vs 75% removed. Both are hedged ('around', '~'); report both, do not average them.

runs.id: E11 -- SVM decision-boundary analysis of the weight state
runs.setup: RBF-kernel SVM trained to classify flattened 6272-dimensional excitatory H→O weight matrices as Task-1-like or Task-2-like, using the last fifth of each single-task training phase [L989-995]. Protocol under test: T1 → T2 → Interleaved_{S,T1}.
runs.numbers: mean signed distance to the decision boundary: Task 1 = -0.069, Task 2 = 0.069, Interleaved_{S,T1} = -0.0047 [L394-396]. For the S5 analogue with Interleaved_{T1,T2}: Task 1 = -0.069, Task 2 = 0.069, Interleaved_{T1,T2} = 0.016 [L1165-1167].
runs.claim: 'the synaptic weight matrices which result from InterleavedS,T1 training are a mixture of Task 1 and Task 2 states' [L418-419]
runs.note: -0.0047 is 6.8% of the 0.069 single-task magnitude; 0.016 is 23%. Taken at face value the sleep-interleaved state sits closer to the boundary (more balanced) than the data-replay-interleaved state -- but the two runs are different protocols and the paper does not compare these two numbers directly.

runs.section: Results L364-403, Fig 4C; S5C for the interleaved analogue
runs.setup: 'task-relevant' synapses are defined as those in the top 10% of the distribution following training on that task [L365-367]. Protocol: T1 → T2 → Interleaved_{S,T1}.
runs.claim: the Task-1-relevant structure is 'destroyed following Task 2 training (top-middle) but partially recovered following InterleavedS,T1 training (top-right)', and the Task-2-relevant structure 'was partially retained following InterleavedS,T1 training' [L374-379]. The word throughout is PARTIALLY.

runs.id: E13 -- Two-cluster synaptic dynamics during sleep-interleaved training
runs.setup: traces of all synapses projecting to a single representative output neuron under T1 → T2 → Interleaved_{S,T1}
runs.numbers: at the onset of Interleaved_{S,T1} (annotated 240,000 aeons) the strong Task-2 cluster ranges from ~0.08 to ~0.4 with the rest grouped near 0 [L453-455]
runs.claim: 'As InterleavedS,T1 training progressed, Task 1 specific synapses moved to the strong cluster and some, presumably less important, Task 2 synapses moved to the weak cluster. After a period of time the rate of transfer decreased and the total number of synapses in each group stabilized, showing that the network approached equilibrium' [L455-485]

runs.id: E14 -- Two-dimensional weight histograms: overwriting vs renormalisation
runs.setup: per-synapse scatter of weight at time slice 1 (x) vs time slice 2 (y), binned. Scale bar: brown = 50 synapses/bin, blue = 1 synapse/bin [L532, L1003-1004].
runs.claim: under T1→T2, 'many strongly trained by Task 1 synapses were depressed down to zero' -- 'complete overwriting of the synaptic weight matrix' [L494-497]. Under T2→Interleaved_{S,T1}, 'many synapses that were strong following Task 2 training were not depressed to zero but rather were pushed to an intermediate strength' [L500-501].
runs.note: This figure is the microscopic evidence for the projection Π of (T04-6): sleep moves weights to an intermediate value rather than to zero.

runs.id: E15 -- Solution-manifold geometry and distance-to-manifold curves
runs.setup: kPCA embeddings of weight configurations from 10 networks; Euclidean distance in the full 6272-dimensional space from the current weight state to the point sets Man_T1, Man_T2 and Man_{T1∩T2}
runs.claim: 'both InterleavedT1,T2 and InterleavedS,T1/T2 training cause synaptic weight configurations to smoothly converge towards MT1∩T2, while Sequential training avoids this intersection entirely' [L573-575]
runs.note: The manifolds are point sets built partly FROM the interleaved runs -- see unfavorable_facts item 11. The authors themselves note under-sampling: '(Note, that we certainly under sampled MT1 and MT2, which may explains initial distance increase.)' [L572-573]

runs.id: E16 -- Receptive fields and the Particle Responsiveness Metric
runs.section: Results L243-262 (single task, Fig 2), L431-446 (post-sleep, Fig 5); S3A-D; Methods: PRM L1037-1095
runs.setup: output-neuron receptive fields computed as the H-to-O-weighted average of hidden-neuron receptive fields [L243-247]; PRM is an author-defined scalar summarising how strongly a particle orientation drives output activity in the matching movement direction
runs.numbers: no scalar values are printed in the text -- only bar plots in S3
runs.claim: after Interleaved_{S,T1} a single upper-left output neuron 'responded to both horizontal (rewarded for Task 1) and vertical (rewarded for Task 2) orientations' [L434-437], and the underlying hidden neurons split into two disjoint task-selective sets [L437-443]
runs.note: This is the paper's mechanistic picture of what a 'joint representation' is: not a blended feature, but two disjoint hidden-neuron subsets multiplexed onto the same decision neuron.

protocol_variants_glossary.Interleaved_{S,T2}: sleep alternated with NEW task (Task 2) training after Task 1; the headline protocol [L300-306, Fig 3E/3F]
protocol_variants_glossary.Interleaved_{S,T1}: sleep alternated with Task 1 training, run AFTER T1→T2 has already erased Task 1; used for all the weight-space analyses [Fig 4, Fig 6]

scale_ceiling.model_size: 842 spiking map-based model neurons in total [L743]: 49 input (7x7), 784 hidden (28x28), 8 functional output (3x3 with a nonfunctional centre) [L744-746]. Plastic parameter count: 7056 input-to-hidden synapses (784 x 9, arithmetic on stated fan-in [L751]) trained once and frozen, plus 6272 excitatory hidden-to-output synapses [L995, L1035] which are the only continuously plastic block. The inhibitory hidden-to-output block is the same size but fully determined [L956-963].
scale_ceiling.token_count: N/A -- no language, no tokens, no text. The input is a 7x7 binary egocentric visual field of a 50x50 grid world with 10% particle density [L731, L739-740].
scale_ceiling.task_count: TWO. This is the hard ceiling of the paper. Both tasks are drawn from the same four-orientation particle vocabulary and are deliberately symmetric complements of one another: Task 1 rewards horizontal and punishes negative diagonal, Task 2 rewards vertical and punishes positive diagonal [L225-226, L231-232]. The paper itself stresses the similarity: 'The similarity between these tasks is evident in their definition (symmetrical particle orientations...), through the similar performances attained by the network on each task ... and through the similar levels of activity induced in the network when training each task' [L233-237]. No three-task sequence, no dissimilar task pair, no task-incremental or class-incremental benchmark.
scale_ceiling.performance_band: Chance is 0.5 and the best single-task performance ever reported is 0.70 ± 0.02 [L167, L228]. The entire dynamic range being protected is therefore 0.20 wide, and the reported standard deviations are 0.02-0.05, i.e. 10-25% of the band.
scale_ceiling.benchmark_provenance: AUTHOR-BUILT. The foraging environment and the rewarded-STDP learning rules are inherited from the same group's prior papers, Sanda, Skorheim & Bazhenov 2017 [ref 14] and Skorheim, Lonjers & Bazhenov 2014 [ref 15] [L862, L799]. The evaluation metric (pattern discriminability) and the secondary metric (PRM) are both defined in this paper [L166-167, L257-259, L1037-1095]. No standard continual-learning benchmark is used -- no permuted MNIST, no split MNIST/CIFAR, no CORe50.
scale_ceiling.compute: NOT STATED. No wall-clock, no CPU-hours, no FLOPs, no code repository in the vendored text. Data Availability says only 'All relevant data are within the paper and its Supporting Information files' [L50-52].
scale_ceiling.learning_algorithm_ceiling: The mechanism is demonstrated ONLY for local spike-timing-dependent plasticity with reward modulation, homeostatic synaptic scaling and heterosynaptic normalisation in a three-layer feedforward spiking network. It is never demonstrated for gradient descent, for a deep network, for a recurrent network, or for anything trained by backpropagation. The authors point to their own prior transfer of the idea into feedforward ANNs [refs 54-56, L677-679] but run none of it here.
scale_ceiling.summary: Largest demonstration: 2 complementary 4-orientation foraging tasks, 842 neurons, 6272 continuously plastic synapses, 8 actions, 10 trials, one sleep-interleaved phase, performance band 0.50-0.70. Distance to LLM deployment scale is roughly nine orders of magnitude in parameters and infinite in kind, since no gradient is ever computed.

extended_or_renamed.note: The paper takes CLS-era interleaved training [refs 4, 10, 11] and removes its data-storage precondition, arguing that the two are 'effectively equivalent': 'interleaving new task training with sleep was effectively equivalent to explicit interleaved training of the old and new tasks without the need to store and train on previous task data or environments' [L610-611]

The paper uses 'replay' in the biological reactivation sense (spontaneous, generated by the network) and explicitly distinguishes it from the deep-learning sense reviewed in ref 9, which involves 'storing a subset of previous veridical inputs and mixing them with more recent inputs' [L673-674]. The monograph must keep these two senses apart; the whole Θ-path hinges on which one is meant.

recast from 'the old task's accuracy dropped' to 'the weight state jumped from one solution manifold to another while avoiding their intersection' [L644-646, L578-583]. This is the paper's conceptual contribution and the reason it belongs in the monograph rather than merely in a citation list.

retired_or_argued_against.term: perpetual storage of original training data
retired_or_argued_against.note: framed as 'the stringent constraint' that interleaved training imposes and that this paper exists to remove [L109-111, L284-286, L674-677]
retired_or_argued_against.source: Introduction L106-113; Results L283-286; Discussion L671-677

retired_or_argued_against.term: synapse freezing (and by explicit extension the EWC family) as a sufficient mechanism
retired_or_argued_against.note: empirically dominated by sleep on both axes at every tested freezing fraction, and argued to be qualitatively the wrong shape of intervention: 'the sleep-like phase performs a significantly more sophisticated modification to the weight matrix than simply freezing (or amplifying) task relevant synapses' [L509-511]. EWC [ref 7] is named as the machine-learning instance of the freezing idea [L517-547].

retired_or_argued_against.term: the claim that sleep's benefit depends on structured, task-specific replay cues
retired_or_argued_against.note: retired by the paper's own control: uniform population-mean noise works as well as per-neuron rate-matched noise [L355-362, S4E/F L1144-1150]

open_questions.q: Does the mechanism survive past two tasks? The paper never runs a third task, so the per-round degradation rate ρ over repeated sleep rounds is entirely unmeasured. The paper's geometric story predicts progressive shrinkage of the intersection region as tasks accumulate, but it neither states nor tests that prediction.
open_questions.source: task set fixed at two throughout, L164-165, L225-232; no multi-task experiment exists in the paper or supplement

open_questions.q: How much uninterrupted new-task training is survivable? The paper identifies a failure regime and never locates its boundary: 'a single episode of new task training using reinforcement learning could quickly erase old memories to the point that they cannot be recovered by subsequent sleep' [L639-640] and 'a single long episode of new task learning would push the network far away from the old task manifold making it impossible to recover by subsequent sleep' [L651-653]. The 100-movement-cycle interval is asserted, never justified or swept.

Is the general continual-learning problem solved? The paper opens by declaring it open [L103-105] and does not close it. Its own scope statement restricts the claim: 'at least for procedural memories that are directly encoded to the cortical network connectivity during new training' [L722-723].

Does the mechanism transfer to gradient-trained networks? The authors assert transfer by citation to their own prior work -- 'we recently successfully implemented a similar approach in feedforward ANNs, where sleep-like phase prevented catastrophic forgetting and improved generalization and adversarial robustness [54-56]' [L677-679] -- but run no such experiment here. Whether the local-plasticity ingredients (heterosynaptic normalisation, homeostatic scaling, eligibility traces) are load-bearing or incidental is left open.

Are mixed-task replays real in this model? The theoretical argument for sleep's superiority over classical interleaving rests on them -- 'Sleep, on the other hand, can support not only replays of the old task, but also support replays which are a mixture of both tasks [41,52,53]. Thus, through unsupervised plasticity during sleep replay, the system is able to perform approximate optimization for the desired dual-task (or multi-task) state.' [L668-670] -- but no analysis of replay content is performed. The claim is imported by citation, not demonstrated.

Only REM-like sleep is modelled. 'to simulate REM sleep-like activity in the model, the rewarded STDP rule was replaced by unsupervised STDP' [L293-295] and the justification is that REM cortical activity is 'low-synchronized and similar to baseline awake activity' [L292-293]. NREM, characterised by 'complex patterns of synchronized neuronal activity' [L719], is not modelled at all -- yet the literature the paper cites assigns declarative-memory consolidation to NREM [L120-122, L627-629]. What NREM-like synchronised replay would add is left open.

The biological prediction is untested. 'Our study predicts synaptic level mechanisms of how sleep-based memory reactivation can protect old memory traces during training of a new interfering memory task.' [L721-722] No in-vivo or in-vitro validation accompanies the paper.

Is the freezing baseline fairly represented? Only three freezing fractions (1%, 5%, 10%) with a single selection criterion (top-magnitude after Task 1) are tested, and EWC -- named as the machine-learning member of this family [L546-547] -- is never actually run. Whether a properly implemented importance-weighted regulariser closes the gap is open.

Does the result depend on the reward asymmetry? Reward is +1 and punishment is -0.001, three orders of magnitude smaller [L932-936]. During sleep the constant is +0.5 -- half the magnitude of the wake reward. No sensitivity analysis over these constants appears.

unfavorable_facts.fact: The strong baseline nearly matches the method, and the paper's own superiority claim is admitted to be theoretical rather than empirical. Interleaved_{T1,T2} (which requires stored old-task data) reaches 0.68 ± 0.03 / 0.65 ± 0.04; sleep reaches 0.70 ± 0.03 / 0.68 ± 0.05. The paper writes 'exceeding those achieved through InterleavedT1,T2 training' [L305-306] on gaps of 0.02 and 0.03 against standard deviations of 0.03-0.05, and then concedes in the Discussion: 'Although classical interleaved training of the old and new tasks showed similar performance results in our model as interleaving new task training with sleep, we believe the latter to be superior on the following theoretical grounds.' [L654-655]. The demonstrated advantage of sleep in this paper is the ELIMINATION OF STORED DATA, not accuracy.

No statistical test appears anywhere in the paper. All numbers are mean ± std over 'at least 10 trials' [L168-169]. The word 'significantly' is used at least three times -- 'fell significantly closer to the decision boundary' [L418], 'significantly below that seen after InterleavedS,T2' [L506], 'significantly driven by these rewarded food particle orientations' [L444] -- with no test named and no p-value reported.

The manifold result is partly definitional. Methods states that the point sets Man_T1 and Man_T2 'included the synaptic weight states from the last fifth of training on a particular task ... and all of the synaptic weight states from the last fifth of both InterleavedT1,T2 and InterleavedS,T1/T2 training', and that 'The intersection of the two solution manifolds (i.e. the point-set MT1∩T2) was defined solely by the synaptic weight states from the last fifth of both InterleavedT1,T2 and InterleavedS,T1 training.' [L1013-1019]. The intersection point set is therefore CONSTRUCTED FROM the interleaved runs whose convergence toward it is then plotted in Fig 7F. This does not make the accuracy results wrong, but the geometric headline -- 'sleep pushes the weight state toward the intersection of the manifolds' -- is not an independent measurement of those trajectories. The monograph must state this when it reproduces Fig 7.
unfavorable_facts.source: Methods: Distance from solution manifolds L1012-1035; Fig 7D-F L567-575

unfavorable_facts.fact: The authors themselves flag under-sampling of the manifolds: '(Note, that we certainly under sampled MT1 and MT2, which may explains initial distance increase.)' [L572-573]. The minimum-distance estimator of (T04-7) is biased upward under sparse sampling in 6272 dimensions.

The sleep phase is not fully information-free with respect to wake. The Poisson drive rates during sleep are computed from firing statistics recorded during preceding training of BOTH tasks: 'we recorded average spiking rates of neurons in the hidden layer H during preceding training of both Task 1 and Task 2; these task specific spiking rates were then averaged to generate target spiking rates' [L982-985]. The paper runs three controls to argue this is not training in disguise [L346-362, S4], and the Uniform-Noise control reduces the carried state to one population-mean scalar [L355-362, L1144-1150] -- but the MAIN configuration whose numbers are the headline does consume 784 wake-derived scalars.
unfavorable_facts.source: Methods: Simulated sleep L981-985; controls Results L341-362 and S4 L1132-1150

unfavorable_facts.fact: Results and Methods describe the sleep-time learning rule in two different vocabularies. Results: 'the rewarded STDP rule was replaced by unsupervised STDP' [L294-295], restated in Methods: Simulated sleep as 'We also change the learning rule between the hidden and output layer from rewarded to unsupervised STDP' [L978-979]. Methods: Synaptic plasticity: 'During periods of sleep the network received a constant reward of Srp = 0.5 on each movement cycle.' [L936-937]. Both sentences are in the paper. A reader given only the first will not expect a positive scalar multiplying every trace during sleep. [The two are reconcilable -- constant modulation is unmodulated Hebbian learning up to scale -- but that reconciliation is MY INFERENCE, not the paper's statement.]

Two tasks only, and they are deliberately symmetric complements from the same four-orientation vocabulary. The paper stresses the similarity as a feature [L233-237]. There is no dissimilar-task pair, no task sequence longer than two, and hence no measurement of ρ over repeated sleep rounds -- the exact quantity the monograph's cost table needs.

The performance band being protected is narrow. Chance is 0.5 and the trained ceiling is 0.70 ± 0.02 [L167, L228-229]. Every claim in the paper lives inside a 0.20-wide interval with per-condition standard deviations of 0.02-0.05.

Author-built task, author-built metric, no standard benchmark. The foraging environment and the rewarded-STDP rules come from the same group's prior work [refs 14, 15, cited at L799 and L862], and both evaluation metrics (pattern discriminability and PRM) are defined in this paper [L166-167, L1037-1095]. No permuted-MNIST, split-MNIST/CIFAR or any other community continual-learning benchmark is run.

Sleep preserves; it does not restore. The mechanism is explicitly conditional on the old trace surviving: 'if Task 1 synapses are still strong enough to maintain replay, they are replayed and weights are increased' [L310-311], and 'a single episode of new task training using reinforcement learning could quickly erase old memories to the point that they cannot be recovered by subsequent sleep' [L639-640]. This bounds the claim sharply: the offline phase does something a wake phase cannot only within a window where the wake damage is still partial.

Freezing is dominated but the comparison is only three points wide, and EWC is cited rather than run. Freeze-1%: 0.54/0.68. Freeze-5%: 0.65/0.61. Freeze-10%: 0.70/0.53 [L1184-1187]. Only top-magnitude-after-Task-1 selection is tested. EWC [ref 7] is named as the ML instance of this family [L517-547] and never implemented.

The paper contains at least three internal inconsistencies a careful reader will hit. (i) Naming: the uniform-noise experiment is 'InterleavedUS,T1' at L359 but 'InterleavedUS,T2' in the S4 caption at L1146; the reported numbers (Task 1 0.67 ± 0.05, Task 2 0.69 ± 0.03) show Task 2 was the trained task. (ii) Dropout threshold: 'around 70% of the hidden layer was pruned' [L241] versus 'remains high until ~25% of neurons are left' [L1109-1110]. (iii) A misprinted standard deviation: 'single Task 1 (0.70 ± 002)' [L305], correct value 0.70 ± 0.02 from L228.

Zero cost accounting. No FLOPs, no wall-clock, no CPU-hours, no memory footprint, no energy, no code link. B_s exists only as a simulated-time duration and is a single unswept point (100 movement cycles, 1:1 duty with wake).
unfavorable_facts.source: absence throughout; Data Availability L50-52; duty ratio L301-303, L985-986

unfavorable_facts.fact: Only 6272 synapses of the final layer are consolidated. The input-to-hidden block is trained once during the 'developmental critical period' and then frozen for every reinforcement-learning phase [L205-207]; during sleep the input layer is silenced so no I→H plasticity can occur at all [L966-967]. All of the paper's claims about sleep are claims about one fully-connected output layer.

The authors state the blank-slate limitation themselves. 'In our model, and indeed in all neural network models, the system begins as a "blank slate" without knowledge of any previous learning or competing demands. In contrast, animals under experimental training paradigms have a wealth of experiences which would serve as priors' [L685-689], and they therefore restrict the claim: 'Due to this stark differences, we focus our attention on the interference phenomena which follow training on an initial task as opposed to initial learning.' [L696-697]

The equations are unnumbered and one of them is not fully recoverable from the vendored text. The precise algebraic form of Δ_m (whether Sum_tr/Avg_tr divides or multiplies) cannot be resolved from L879-925 as rendered. Two other constants, δ and Δ_tar, are introduced without numeric values.

not_evidence_for_llms.preamble: This paper is the corpus's strongest DIRECT evidence that an offline phase produces a weight state no wake phase produces. That claim must be stated precisely, because it is easy to over-transfer. What follows is the boundary.
what_it_IS_evidence_for: That a network can be made to replay its own past task WITHOUT any stored past data, and that the replay is sufficient to hold old-task performance at its trained value (0.70 ± 0.03 versus 0.70 ± 0.02) while a new task is learned to its own trained value (0.68 ± 0.05 versus 0.69 ± 0.03) [L228-229, L276, L304-305].

That the replay source can be structureless: uniform population-mean Poisson noise works as well as per-neuron rate-matched noise [L355-362, S4E/F L1144-1150]. The wake→sleep carried state can be one scalar.
That the offline phase is not equivalent to any static protection of the old parameters: every tested freezing fraction is dominated on both axes simultaneously [S6 L1181-1189 versus L304-305].
That interleaving GRANULARITY matters and there is a regime boundary: short training episodes alternated with sleep succeed where one long episode is unrecoverable [L307-311, L639-642, L649-653].

That the resulting weight state is genuinely intermediate, by three independent readouts -- SVM distance to the decision boundary (-0.0047 versus ±0.069) [L394-396], PC-space location [Fig 4E], and per-synapse 2-D histograms showing old-task synapses pushed to intermediate rather than zero strength [Fig 6D right, L500-502].
what_it_is_NOT_evidence_for: NOT evidence about gradient-trained networks. There is no loss function, no derivative, no optimizer, and no backward pass anywhere in this paper. The write rule is a local eligibility-gated Hebbian product followed by a hard normalisation projection [(T04-2), (T04-6)]. Nothing licenses the inference that an SGD/AdamW sleep round on an LLM inherits these dynamics.

NOT evidence about transformers, language, or sequence modelling. The network is a three-layer feedforward spiking classifier over a 7x7 binary field with 8 actions. No attention, no recurrence, no tokens.
NOT evidence at deployment scale. 6272 continuously plastic synapses versus 10^9-10^12 parameters. Two tasks versus open-ended task streams.

NOT evidence that the replay content is semantically correct. The paper never inspects what is replayed; the mixed-task-replay argument is imported by citation [L668-670, refs 41/52/53]. In an LLM the analogous failure -- replay that is fluent but false -- is the central risk of the Θ-path and this paper says nothing about it.

NOT evidence that sleep beats data replay on quality. Classical interleaved training with stored data performs within one standard deviation [L282 versus L304-305]. If the old data is available, this paper gives no accuracy reason to prefer sleep.
NOT evidence about ρ over repeated rounds. Two tasks, one Interleaved phase. Any statement about how many sleep rounds a model can sustain is unsupported by this paper.
NOT evidence about serving cost. No FLOPs, no latency, no bytes, no batching, no hardware. The 1:1 sleep:wake duty ratio is a modelling choice in simulated time, not a compute budget.

CRITICALLY: the mechanism depends on machinery transformers do not have -- spike timing as the correlation signal, per-neuron firing-rate homeostasis with target rates, heterosynaptic normalisation enforcing constant column sums, balanced feedforward inhibition, and a 6-movement-cycle eligibility trace [L861-963]. The paper's own account of why sleep beats freezing rests on the normalisation constraint [L509-517]. Remove the constraint and the argument has no stated substitute.
not_evidence_for_llms.the_one_transferable_structural_claim: R_k in frame Eq. (U-Θ) does not have to be a dataset. It can be a stream generated by running the model on noise, with H_k stored nowhere but in Θ_k. This paper demonstrates that this is sufficient for retention in at least one system, and that the auxiliary state required to seed the generation can be a single scalar. Every other transfer to LLMs is an analogy and must be marked as one.

cross_path_citations.verdict: Total silence toward the E path and the W path, and the silence is chronologically forced rather than chosen. The paper was published 2022-11-18 [L36], before every E-path paper in the corpus (MemGPT 2023, Letta STC 2025) and every W-path paper. Its 77 references are neuroscience, psychology, spiking-network modelling, and the classical connectionist forgetting literature. A grep of the full text for 'transformer', 'language model', 'attention' (in the architectural sense), 'LoRA', 'retrieval', 'generative replay', 'fast weight', 'test-time' and 'prompt' returns nothing but false positives on ordinary English usage. There is no arXiv preprint of this paper and no code link in the vendored text.

W_path.note: No fast weights, no test-time training, no memory-augmented networks, no MAML, no RNN/SSM state, no attention. E_path.note: The only external store that appears is 'the original training data ... perpetually stored for later use' [L109-111] and the DL replay buffer of 'storing a subset of previous veridical inputs' [L673-674]. Both are named as the cost this paper exists to remove. There is no vector store, no retrieval, no knowledge base, no agent memory. Chronology makes this unremarkable -- MemGPT postdates this paper by eleven months -- but the ARGUMENT is not merely absent, it is adverse: the paper's stated value proposition is that the external store is unnecessary.

cross_path_citations.finding_for_the_monograph: This paper is the biological ancestor that NONE of the three paths inherits from in writing within this corpus's own citation graph as seen from this end. It states its problem in the vocabulary of 1995 CLS and 2017 EWC, it answers it with 2007-era spiking machinery, and it hands the result forward without ever naming a language model. When the monograph writes its bridge chain, the honest statement is: the Θ path's later members carry this paper's METAPHOR (sleep, replay, consolidation) but this paper carries none of their MACHINERY, and the transfer of authority from here to there has to be justified by the later papers, not by this one.

systems_implications.framing_warning: The paper contains NO hardware, NO cost model and NO serving context. Everything in this section is either (a) a count the paper states, or (b) an inference explicitly marked as mine. Per the NM D4 rule inherited by S0-DESIGN, no memory-hierarchy argument is licensed by this paper and the monograph must not manufacture one.
systems_implications.decode_cost: Unchanged by sleep. [PAPER-STATED basis] a decision is one movement cycle of 600 simulation timesteps through the fixed 7x7 → 28x28 → 3x3 feedforward path [L744-746, L769, L776-789]; sleep alters only the values in Θ^{H→O} [L978-980]. [INFERENCE] Therefore the sleep-time compute of this paper buys retention at exactly zero wake-time cost -- the ideal shape for the amortization argument -- but the paper measures neither side, so it contributes no number to Eq. (A).
systems_implications.state_bytes: [PAPER-STATED counts, NO dtype and NO byte figure anywhere] 6272 excitatory hidden-to-output synapses [L995, L1035]; 6272 inhibitory synapses that are fully determined by the excitatory ones and are therefore not independent state [L956-963]; 8 homeostatic set-point scalars [L938-945]; 784 fixed outgoing-sum targets [L928-930]; 784 measured sleep-drive rates [L982-985], reduced to 1 by the Uniform-Noise control [L1144-1150]. [PAPER-STATED, and the number that matters] ZERO bytes of past-task data [L611, L674-677, L727].
systems_implications.the_capacity_result_worth_carrying: [INFERENCE from paper-stated facts] The state that must cross the wake→sleep boundary is O(1) scalars, not O(dataset). If that property survives transfer to a gradient-trained model -- which this paper does not establish -- it would mean a Θ-path sleep round needs no per-user replay buffer at all, only the weights themselves. That is the single systems claim the monograph is entitled to draw from here, and it must be drawn as a hypothesis, not a result.
systems_implications.batching_consequence: [INFERENCE -- the paper has one agent and never discusses serving] Because both wake and sleep write the same deployed weight block, this architecture has no frozen serving artefact. Translated into the Rosetta table of STC-STYLE-NOTATION §3, 'batch with shared weights' breaks completely: every agent's weights diverge from the first movement cycle. This is the extreme end of the Θ-path's per-user-delta problem, and it is worth stating precisely because it shows the problem is intrinsic to the path and not an artefact of LoRA-style implementations.
systems_implications.duty_cycle: [PAPER-STATED] Sleep and wake intervals are both 100 movement cycles, a 1:1 ratio in simulated time [L301-303, L985-986]. [INFERENCE] In Eq. (A) terms this is C_sleep = C_wake per period with N_q undefined, so no break-even N_q* can be computed. The monograph should say so explicitly rather than leaving the cell blank.
systems_implications.where_the_traffic_lands: Not addressed and not inferable. The paper reports no memory footprint, no arithmetic intensity, no data movement, and no hardware target. Any statement placing this workload in HBM, DRAM or anywhere else would be invented.
systems_implications.the_shape_of_the_sleep_workload: [INFERENCE from Methods] The sleep round is: (i) generate independent Poisson spike trains for 784 hidden units; (ii) propagate through a dense 784x8 matrix for 60,000 timesteps; (iii) apply local trace updates and, after every event, a column-wise renormalisation of the same 784x8 matrix. It is small, dense, sequential in time, and dominated by the per-event normalisation rather than by the matrix product. That profile is the OPPOSITE of an LLM sleep round (large, batched, gradient-dominated) and the monograph should use the contrast to make the point that 'offline compute' names a schedule, not a workload shape.
systems_implications.the_one_number_a_systems_reader_can_take: 0.70 → 0.52 without sleep, 0.70 → 0.70 with a 1:1 sleep duty cycle and zero stored data [L228-229, L275, L304-305]. Everything else in this paper is mechanism, not cost.
